To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

blockade of ion‐otropic glutamate receptors triggers a cascade of events that leads to neuronal apoptosis through the mitochondrial death pathway, and that Ca2+ deficiency is a key factor in this process.

Blockade of ion‐otropic glutamate receptors (NMDA and non‐NMDA receptors) produces neuronal apoptosis via the Bax‐Cytochrome c‐Caspase pathway, the causative role is Ca2+ deficiency, and this pathway is activated by the sequential mitochondrial death signals.
the blockade of ionotropic receptors induces neuronal apoptosis through the mitochondrial death pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca2+, caspases and the mitochondrial death pathway in neuronal apoptosis induced by the blockade of ionotropic receptors.
the role of Ca2+, the Bax‐Cytochrome C‐Caspase pathway, and the involvement of caspase-3 in neuronal apoptosis induced by glutamate antagonists.
the molecular mechanisms by which ionotropic glutamate antagonists cause neuronal apoptosis in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blockade of ionotropic receptors causes neuronal apoptosis through a mitochondria‐mediate death pathway, which includes the Bax‐Cytochrome C‐Caspase pathway.
glutamate antagonists induce neuronal cell death through the Bax–cytochrome C–caspase‐3 pathway.
blockade of glutamate receptors causes neuronal cell death through the Bax–cytochrome C–caspase pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glutamate‐induced neuronal death occurs through two different pathways, one involving the activation of ion channels and the other involving glutamate receptors.
glutamate antagonists induce caspase‐mediated neuronal cell apoptosis through a mitochondria‐mediatied pathway.
glutamate antagonists induce caspase‐mediated neuronal death by Ca2+ deficiency, which is linked to the mitochondrial pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of caspasedependent apoptotic pathways in cortical neurons is due to a deficiency in intracellular Ca2+ levels.
blockade of ionotrophic glutamate receptors causes Ca2+ deficiency, leading to the sequential mitochondrial pathway of neuronal apoptosis.
